summary: Design affordable climate and livelihood covers with pricing, data, partnerships, and governance tools. Build a practical pilot plan with TrainingCred.
lede: Microinsurance and parametric insurance design for agriculture, MSMEs, and climate risk helps you turn customer and value-chain risks into suitable, financially viable products. You will learn to define perils and benefits, assess affordability, use credible exposure data for basic pricing, and manage basis risk in parametric payouts. Through practical exercises, you will create a customer-risk map, product specification, exposure-data register, pricing workbook, distribution scorecard, and regulatory review checklist. You will also calculate premium components in Microsoft Excel, test triggers against historical or sample weather data, prepare partner operating models, and use Power BI for a guided portfolio and payout dashboard exercise with no programming required.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who shape, finance, regulate, distribute, or evaluate insurance solutions for low-income households, small enterprises, farmers, and climate-exposed communities. It suits beginner to intermediate practitioners who understand their institution’s operating context and need a structured product development method.
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to insurance, microfinance, agricultural programmes, social protection, or disaster risk management. Basic numeracy and spreadsheet use will help, but actuarial qualification, programming, and prior parametric insurance implementation are not required. You should bring a laptop with spreadsheet software; the exercises use provided sample data and templates. Advanced climate analytics and regulatory interpretation receive operational application or conceptual awareness treatment, not technical engineering depth.
